runs.text: The ordinary generating function of a sequence stores its nth term as the coefficient of x to the n. In formal-power-series work, x is an indeterminate and algebra is justified coefficient by coefficient without evaluating an infinite sum.
Multiplying a recurrence by x to the n and summing over its valid range converts shifts into powers of x. Initial terms become boundary corrections, often leaving a rational expression for A.

items.text: State the starting index. An OGF beginning at n = 0 differs from one beginning at n = 1 by its constant term and every shift correction.
Formal identities require the denominator's constant term to be invertible. If x is evaluated numerically, analytic convergence conditions must be checked separately.
When summing a recurrence, begin at the first index where it is valid and retain all omitted initial terms.

items.text: Dropping initial-condition corrections is the most common source of a wrong numerator.
The Cauchy product gives a convolution, not termwise multiplication of coefficients.
Do not impose a radius-of-convergence restriction during purely formal coefficient extraction; do impose it when treating the series as a numerical function.
